resources.string: Scans run on this phone. Nothing is monitored in the background; you decide what to check.
Cloud checks: on (only when you tap them)
Analyse a suspicious SMS or chat message
Inspect a web address before opening it
Scan QR codes and UPI payment requests
Read a screenshot’s text on this phone and analyse it
No scans yet. Your results will appear here.
You never need to enter a UPI PIN or scan a QR code to receive money.
Banks never ask for your OTP, PIN, CVV or password by call, SMS or WhatsApp.
Police and agencies never conduct “digital arrests” over video calls.
KYC is updated only in your bank’s official app or branch, never through an SMS link.
Do not install AnyDesk, TeamViewer or APK files because a caller asks you to.
Lost money to fraud? Call 1930 immediately or report at cybercrime.gov.in.
Lost money? Call 1930 or visit cybercrime.gov.in
Paste a suspicious SMS, WhatsApp message or offer. It is analysed on this phone.
Could not read text from this image.
No text was found in this image.
Text read from your screenshot on this phone. Check it for recognition errors.
Shared content loaded. Review it, then analyse.
Paste a link to inspect it without opening it.
You are about to leave CyberShield and open:\n%1$s
This shows high-risk signals. Continue only if you are certain it is genuine.
No app on this phone can open this.
Result from on-device rules. It is not proof that something is malicious or safe.
Result from on-device rules and the experimental AI model. It is not proof that something is malicious or safe.
Only this link’s address is sent to the CyberShield server, which looks it up in Google Safe Browsing, VirusTotal and URLhaus. Nothing else leaves your phone.

Numbers, e-mail addresses, UPI IDs and link parameters are removed first. The text below is sent to the CyberShield server and to Google Gemini to generate an explanation. CyberShield does not store it.
This exact text will be sent:
Allow cloud checks when I tap them (you can turn this off in Settings)
Cloud checks are not set up for this build. Local analysis still works.
Could not reach the CyberShield server. Local analysis still works.
Too many requests. Try again in a minute.
No connected provider lists this link as a threat. New scam sites are often not listed yet, so this does not prove it is safe.
No threat-intelligence provider could answer right now.
No threat-intelligence provider is configured on this server yet, so only the on-device result above applies.
Generated by AI. It can be wrong. Use official channels for decisions.
Scan a code, inspect what it contains, then decide. Nothing opens automatically.
Camera access is requested only when you choose to scan a QR code. Frames are processed on this phone.
No QR code was found in this image.
The camera could not start. Close other camera apps, or scan a QR from an image.
Paying with UPI always takes money FROM your account. You never need to scan a code or enter a PIN to receive money.
Your UPI app will show a payment to %1$s. Check the payee name and amount there before entering your PIN. CyberShield never makes payments.
Stored only on this phone. Message text, full links, UPI IDs and numbers are never saved.
History saving is turned off in Settings.
This permanently removes every scan record from this phone.
Detection always checks English, Hindi and Marathi phrases, whatever language you choose.
Allow cloud checks when I tap them
Off by default. Nothing is ever sent automatically.

Adds a trained on-device check that can raise the risk level for messages whose wording looks like a scam, even when no rule matches. Runs entirely on your phone. Off by default while it is being evaluated.
No AI model is bundled in this build yet, so this setting has no effect.

Send this redacted message to help improve scam detection. It is submitted as a suspected scam. Personal details have been removed (shown below) and nothing identifies you. This needs the backend to be configured, and happens only when you tap Send.
Don\'t ask again before donating (you can turn this off in Settings)
Thanks. Your redacted sample was sent to help improve detection.
No server configured. Cloud checks are unavailable.
Release builds only accept https:// server addresses.
Save scan history on this phone
This deletes scan history and all settings on this phone.
Messages, links, QR codes and screenshots are analysed on this phone by default.
Cloud checks run only when you tap them and agree. A link check sends only the link. An AI explanation sends text with personal numbers and IDs removed.
CyberShield does not read your SMS inbox, chats or notifications, and does not monitor other apps.
The camera is used only on the QRGuard screen. Screenshots are read only when you pick or share them.
A low score does not prove that a message or website is safe.
Uses urgency or pressure to rush you.
Threatens that an account, card or SIM will be blocked or suspended.
Threatens to cut electricity, gas or mobile service unless you act now.
Asks you to share an OTP. Banks and UPI apps never ask for it.
Asks for a UPI PIN or MPIN. You only type it into your own UPI app to send money.
Asks for card number, CVV or expiry date.
Asks for a password or net-banking login.
Mentions an OTP, PIN, CVV or password.
Claims you must enter a PIN, scan a QR or approve a request to RECEIVE money. A UPI PIN is only needed to send money.
Pushes you to make or approve a payment.
Asks you to update or verify KYC, PAN or Aadhaar details.
Promises a prize, lottery, reward or cashback.
Offers a refund that you must claim.
Advertises an instant or pre-approved loan.
Offers easy work-from-home or task-based income, a common prepaid-task scam.
Promises guaranteed or unusually high returns.
Asks for an upfront fee, deposit or charge.
Invokes police, CBI, customs or courts, as “digital arrest” scams do.
Asks you to install a screen-sharing or remote-access app such as AnyDesk.
Asks you to install an APK file from outside the Play Store.
Asks you to keep this secret or stay on the call.
Asks you to call or message a number given in the text.
Contains a link. Its destination was checked separately below.
Contains a link with risky characteristics.
Its wording resembles known scams, even without a specific red-flag phrase.
This is not a complete web address with a host.
Uses a link type that can run code or open apps directly.
The address had no http:// or https://; it was checked as https://.
Does not use HTTPS, so the connection is not encrypted.
Hides text before an @ sign that can disguise the real website.
Uses a raw IP address instead of a website name.
The website name contains encoded characters.
The website name uses international (punycode) characters. Check its spelling carefully.
The website name mixes alphabets, a look-alike trick.
Uses a well-known brand name, but the website is not owned by that brand.
The website name looks like a misspelling of a well-known brand.
Uses a link shortener that hides where it really goes.
Hosted on a free website service often used for throwaway scam pages.
Uses a domain ending that is often abused for scams.
Contains words such as login, verify or KYC that are common in fake links.
Has an unusually long chain of sub-domains.
The website name has several hyphens.
Downloads an Android APK file directly.
Contains another web address that can redirect you elsewhere.
The QR code is empty or unreadable.
The QR code contains only text, not a link or payment.
The QR code triggers an action such as a call, SMS, e-mail, Wi-Fi or contact.
This is a UPI payment code. Paying SENDS money from your account.
The UPI request has no valid payee address.
The payee UPI ID is malformed.
This is a collect request: approving it takes money out of your account.
The amount is pre-filled. Check it before paying.
The payee name or note mentions refunds, prizes, KYC or receiving money.
The payee name claims to be a bank, government body or customer care.
The payment currency is not Indian rupees.
The UPI handle is not a common bank or app handle.
Never share OTPs, UPI PINs, CVVs or passwords with anyone, even callers who say they are from your bank.
You never need a UPI PIN or a QR scan to receive money. Decline the request.
Do not open the link. Type the official website address yourself.
Contact the organisation through its official app, website or the number on your card, not the contact in this message.
Do not install apps or APK files sent by others. Uninstall any screen-sharing app a stranger asked you to install.
Real prizes, jobs and loans never ask you to pay a fee first.
Police and government agencies do not arrest people on video calls or ask for money to close a case. Hang up.
Check the payee name and amount in your UPI app before entering your PIN.
If money was lost, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in immediately.
Report fraudulent calls, SMS or WhatsApp messages on the Sanchar Saathi “Chakshu” portal.
No strong red flags were found on this phone. Still verify the sender before acting.
Report fraud calls, SMS and WhatsApp messages on Chakshu. If you have lost money, call 1930 now or file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
OTPs and your card, account and Aadhaar numbers were removed. The sender’s phone number, UPI ID and links are kept because they identify the scammer. Check the text before you share it.
Copied. Paste it into the complaint form.
Before you pay with a QR code
Check that the payee name in your UPI app is the person or shop you mean to pay.
In shops and parking lots, check that a new QR sticker has not been pasted over the original.
